{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRkquM8AAAABahtY_w", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5zhEIMjE", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5", "number": 107, "title": "Implement PPU raster-progress rendering and mid-scanline register effects", "body": "## Problem

The SNES emulation core has substantial scanline-based PPU coverage, but **`ppu-raster` is explicitly unimplemented**. In current `main` (`a0435c7699bf1f58cf8946d99d4d21d91337b80f`), `SystemBus::tick` invokes `Ppu::render_line(y)` once on crossing HBlank (H=1096). `render_line` then samples the current register state to draw the **entire** visible line. A CPU or DMA write to a display-affecting register partway through a line cannot affect only the pixels that follow it: depending on when the line is rendered, it changes all pixels or none.

That prevents faithful mid-scanline raster effects and is a key architectural limitation for compatibility with a wider range of SNES games.

Relevant baseline:
- [PPU scanline renderer](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/a0435c7699bf1f58cf8946d99d4d21d91337b80f/crates/snes-core/src/ppu.rs)
- [Master-clock scheduler / HBlank rendering](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/a0435c7699bf1f58cf8946d99d4d21d91337b80f/crates/snes-core/src/machine.rs)
- [Implemented features and limits](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/README.md#implemented-features-and-limits)

## Expected outcome

Implement a **first complete, testable raster-rendering foundation** for ordinary NTSC non-interlaced SNES display, so that CPU-originated and DMA/HDMA-originated PPU changes at distinct times within **one visible scanline** affect the appropriate later pixels, **without retroactively changing already emitted pixels**.

The first supported live-effect contract must include:
1. `INIDISP` (`$2100`) forced-blank and brightness changes within a visible line.
2. At least one independently observable **non-INIDISP** mid-line effect using existing rendering logic (e.g. fixed color via `COLDATA` / `$2132`, or a clearly sourced color-math/window enable change) so the implementation is not a special case that only toggles display blanking.
3. Correct prior-pixel preservation and end-of-line completion for ordinary 256-pixel low-resolution lines; preservation of existing 512-pixel hires/pseudo-hires output and framebuffer/Wasm API.

This Issue establishes **raster-aware output**, not a claim of fully dot-accurate VRAM fetch, OAM evaluation, bus arbitration, or all PPU effects. Build on the existing Rust PPU; do not import an emulator core or add game-specific visual hacks.

## Context and implementation scope

- [ ] Reconcile the relevant display-dot vs master-clock schedule using [Fullsnes](https://problemkaputt.de/fullsnes.htm), [SNESdev Timing](https://snes.nesdev.org/wiki/Timing) and existing documented NTSC long-dot/short-line rules. Record the specific **observable output boundary convention** for a write at/between pixel boundaries (and separate source-backed facts from any provisional choices). Do not substitute PPU dot count directly for CPU HTIME counters.
- [ ] Change the PPU/scheduler interface to advance rendering over the **elapsed portion** of a visible scanline in clock/dot order. Rendering must progress with native CPU instruction/bus cycles and DMA/HDMA timing, including when one `tick` crosses multiple pixel or line boundaries. Do not defer every pixel until HBlank.
- [ ] Ensure register changes update only future output: render up to the correct pre-write boundary before committing relevant PPU register writes. Preserve the existing ordering and deferred DMA/HDMA/IRQ scheduling where unrelated. Explicitly test consecutive writes in the same clock neighborhood and HBlank/VBlank boundaries.
- [ ] Reuse and refactor existing BG/OBJ, window/color-math, palette, geometry and framebuffer code rather than implementing a parallel game-specific renderer. Track already-emitted pixels, line/frame transitions, forced blank, and 256/512 output promotion so no stale pixels leak across lines or frames.
- [ ] Implement the scoped `INIDISP` and additional live color/compositing effect with deterministic output. Define a documented initial subset of Mode 1/other existing non-mosaic/non-interlaced rendering to be covered, without regressing static Mode 0–7/hires behavior already exercised. Do not declare all modes and effects dot-exact merely because the foundation is clock-driven.
- [ ] Add deterministic unit/integration tests based on **independent literal raster/clock expectations**, including a change in the left half vs right half, more than one change on a line, exact before/at/after pixels, forced blank on/off and brightness levels, interleaved colors, line/frame boundary, multiple tick partitions, and a negative case proving the old whole-line renderer would fail.
- [ ] Add at least one **original, source-built, MIT-licensed 65C816 ROM** that programs a mid-line display change through ordinary CPU I/O (not direct host mutation). Run it via the native emulator and actual Wasm/browser path; assert framebuffer output on both sides of the boundary. Where practical, include a DMA- or HDMA-driven update at a known phase and verify that it does not rewrite previous pixels. Keep ROM source and provenance in the existing fixture conventions; do not ship ROMs via GitHub Pages.
- [ ] Add deterministic raster snapshots / relevant test traces for diagnosing regressions, with bounded frames and timeouts. Test frame hashes and whole/irregular/single-clock stepping invariance. Keep the existing clock-driven audio cadence and CPU/PPU/DMA/HDMA synchronization behavior.
- [ ] Update README and a focused `docs/issue-<number>-validation.md` with the precise tested subset, timing assumptions/provisional rules, source references, executed commands, pass/fail evidence, and outstanding chip-accuracy gaps.

### Important implementation boundaries

Keep scope coherent and deliverable: the **visible raster-progress engine and these demonstrated mid-line effects** are required. Do not hold this Issue open for comprehensive sprite pixel-fetch arbitration, exact rendering-owned OAM/CGRAM corruption, mid-line scroll/tilemap fetch latency, full mosaic/offset-per-tile interactions, interlace/overscan, PAL, enhancement chips, save states or commercial-catalog compatibility. Those require separate scoped issues.

When an edge of the chosen display-write timing cannot be established unambiguously from existing documentation, choose a deterministic, **explicitly PROVISIONAL / HARDWARE UNVERIFIED** convention and test against that convention; do not present it as observed physical hardware and do not indefinitely block implementation on an unavailable hardware measurement. If a known test contradicts the provisional rule, fix it rather than masking the failure.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Mid-line PPU writes from a real guest ROM cause a visible split on a single line, with unchanged pixels preceding the event and changed pixels after it; test both forced-blank/brightness and at least one non-INIDISP effect.
- [ ] Results are reproducible with one-clock, irregular and large clock advances, including CPU I/O and DMA/HDMA event boundaries, without double-rendering or missing a line.
- [ ] Existing non-raster frames and documented 256/512 geometry match established golden/framebuffer assertions; live raster updates behave correctly in the scoped low-resolution cases. Existing Castle Platformer and modified Memory Game source-built replays, progression and music/effects continue to pass with unchanged fixture hashes.
- [ ] Original guest test is built from auditable MIT source, includes license/provenance, and demonstrates that it fails against the original scanline-only behavior for a substantive reason. No commercial ROMs, Nintendo firmware, or external emulation code are used.
- [ ] Targeted raster tests, formatting, warning-denying Clippy and `cargo test --workspace --locked` pass. Run relevant [README validation commands](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/README.md#validate): source-built CPU/SPC700 and HDMA fixtures, reproducible cleared-game builds, `npm --prefix web run build`, real Chromium/Playwright checks, and Pages subpath artifact smoke checks. Report actual results, skips and limitations accurately.
- [ ] Document what is **implemented** versus only provisional or still unverified, with clear clock/pixel oracles and follow-up targets. The `ppu-raster` inventory may be marked **partial** when this foundation is demonstrated, but **not fully verified**.

## Optional validation

Additional legal homebrew raster-effect ROMs; visual comparisons with reference-emulator/hardware captures (clearly distinguish corroboration from hardware evidence); benchmarking in additional browsers. No physical-device or unaudited commercial-ROM test is a mandatory approval condition.

## Required post-merge verification

None. The existing `main` GitHub Pages workflow will deploy after merge. Its success is checked in the ordinary deployment workflow; publication of a merge-triggered site cannot be a pre-merge acceptance gate. If a new production-only issue appears, track it in a separate follow-up Issue.

## Related work

The preceding [Issue #105](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/issues/105) documented a provisional H-only IRQ boundary policy. Preserve its tests and avoid conflating CPU IRQ counters with PPU pixel timing.
